messages.body_plain:
The following forum message was posted by tfry at http://sourceforge.net/projects/rkward/forums/forum/165574/topic/4101958:

Hi!

By default, RKWard saves the list of open windows in an object ".rk.workplace.save"
in the .RData file. That object is created directly before saving the workspace,
and is removed after loading the workspace. Thus, if you want to modify the
paths, there, you will need to use a plain R session. In fact, perhaps this
mechanism is not terribly smart, after all, although I don't really have an
idea for something better, ATM.

RKWard can also be configured to save the list of open windows "globally" (i.e.
not per workspace). In this case you will find the relevant paths
in ~/.kde/share/config/rkwardrc .

[quote]Anyway, having the option of relative path would be nice. I would make
it relative to the directory where .RData is.[/quote]

Agreed. This would be very useful (and should be the default). It's on my TODO
list (which keeps growing).

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
The following forum message was posted by tfry at http://sourceforge.net/projects/rkward/forums/forum/165574/topic/4101958:

Hi,

I used to lean against using a separate text file, esp. since this gives a headache
for remote URLs. On the other hand, remote URLs are rare in the first place,
and probably, the workplace representation is meaningless in this case, anyway.
So I decided to go with a separate file, indeed.

As a by-product, there are two new R functions rk.save.workplace() and
rk.restore.workplace(), which might be of interest to power users (these could
be used to switch between several sets of opened script windows).

IIRC, you are using Ubuntu? Then perhaps you may be interested in giving tomorrow's
daily builds a try: https://launchpad.net/~rkward-devel/+archive/rkward-dailys
. Otherwise, you can compile from SVN (http://p.sf.net/rkward/svn).

BTW, the workplace save file now also includes information on the "base" directory
of the current workspace. In case the workspace has moved, for each script file
to restore, RKWard will first try to open it from the old (absolute) location,
and if it does not exist, there, RKWard will try to load it from an adjusted
(relative) location. Thus, future versions should generally be able to cope
with moved directories out of the box, without the need for manual editing.

Regards
Thomas

Probably you installed from source, earlier? Unfortunately, since R looks for
packages in many different locations, installing with different methods has
the potential to end up with a mix of different versions. That's basically what
this error message is about. Looks like I talked you into that situation. Sorry.

[code]R CMD REMOVE rkward[/code]
several times, possibly with "-l /usr/lib/R/library", "-l /usr/lib/R/site-library",

can no longer be found in a plain R session. Now re-install rkward from
synaptic.

Regards
Thomas

Ok, now it makes sense. Well, the problem is that the daily builds are built
against the version of R in the Ubuntu universe. For karmic that's 2.9.2. However,
you have R 2.12.1, probably from CRAN. So that's why R refuses to load it...

Well, that's not easily resolvable. You could upgrade your Ubuntu, you could
compile RKWard from source (http://p.sf.net/rkward/svn for the latest version),
or you could go back to whatever version you had installed, previously.

(Probably at some point we will provide more PPAs on launchpad, which would
cover your setup, too, but probably not for the daily builds.)

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward-announce] New mailing list rkward-announce
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] [rkward-announce] New mailing list rkward-announce
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

This is to announce our new mailing list "rkward-announce". rkward-announce is 
meant to be a very low volume mailing list. The idea is that this list may be 
of interest particularly to packagers. The list will receive notifications of 
new release schedules and new official releases, but rarely anything else.

This list is read-only for most purposes. Any mail you send to it will be 
moderated, and most likely rejected. Reply to rkward-devel or rkward-users, 
instead.

Visit https://lists.sourceforge.net/mailman/listinfo/rkward-announce to 
subscribe.

-- Current subscribers of rkward-users and / or rkward-devel --

If you are happy with the amount and type of mail you get, you do not need to 
change anything. You will automatically receive all mail to rkward-announce. 
There is no benefit in subscribing to rkward-announce *in addition* to rkward-
users or rkward-devel.

-- Current moderators of rkward-devel --

I have made you moderators of rkward-announce, too, with the same password. In 
contrast to rkward-devel, please apply very strict moderation standards to 
rkward-announce. I.e., here, any mail which is not an important announcement 
should be rejected (ideally with an explanation that mail should be sent to 
rkward-users / rkward-devel, instead).

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward-announce] RKWard 0.5.5 release schedule / call for testing
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] [rkward-announce] RKWard 0.5.5 release schedule / call for testing
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

Once again, it's time to release a new version of RKWard. While not too many 
visible features have been added, the current development sources contain a 
sizeable number of bugfixes. Also, there have been significant internal changes: 
RKWard now consists of two separate processes, one for the frontend, one for 
the backend, which helps to iron out some incompatibilities with certain 
packages (rJava, and RGtk2, in particular), and to enhance stability, overall.

Of course, all the changes need to be tested, and so, if you have a bit of 
time to spare, please participate in testing. Details on where to find sources 
and / or binaries of the 0.5.5 pre-releases can be found here:
https://sourceforge.net/apps/mediawiki/rkward/index.php?title=Release_Schedule

The testing phase will be open until March 6, 2011. Please try to provide your 
feedback until then. The targetted official release date for RKWard 0.5.5 is 
March 14, 2011.

-- Translators --

Now is a good time to start updating your translations. As usual, the deadline 
for sending updated translations ends with the testing phase, i.e. March 6, 
2011.

-- Developers --

I have created a separate branch for the release in SVN 
(release_branch_0.5.5). This means, you are free to do any type of changes in 
trunk, as usual. However, if you want a change to become part of the release, 
it will have to be merged into the release branch. Write a mail to rkward-
devel, if unsure.

Regards
Thomas
